TASK ID: vertex-cover-to-clique

USER REQUEST:
Write a polynomial-time reduction from Vertex Cover to Clique. problems.py defines both problems: SOURCE is Vertex Cover and TARGET is Clique. The SOURCE and TARGET class docstrings give the exact instance formats, yes-conditions and edge cases.

PROBLEM DEFINITIONS (the SOURCE and TARGET docstrings from problems.py, complete as given here):

SOURCE = VertexCover
Vertex Cover.

Instance: {"n": n, "edges": [[u, v], ...], "k": k}
  * Vertices are 0..n-1. Edges are undirected pairs [u, v] with u != v;
    [u, v] and [v, u] are the same edge and may not both appear.
  * k is any integer.

Yes iff the graph has a vertex cover of AT MOST k vertices: a set of
vertices that includes at least one endpoint of every edge.

Edge cases: k < 0 is always no. A graph with no edges is yes for every
k >= 0 (the empty set covers it). k >= n is yes, since all vertices cover
every edge.

TARGET = Clique
Clique.

Instance: {"n": n, "edges": [[u, v], ...], "k": k}
  * Vertices are 0..n-1. Edges are undirected pairs [u, v] with u != v;
    [u, v] and [v, u] are the same edge and may not both appear.
  * k is any integer.

Yes iff the graph has a clique of AT LEAST k vertices: k vertices with an
edge between every two of them.

Edge cases: k <= 0 is always yes. k = 1 is yes whenever n >= 1. k > n is
always no.

INPUT FILES: ["problems.py"]
WORKING DIRECTORY: /tmp/reduction-e45pxlsy

The answer to the returned instance must be yes exactly when the answer to the input instance is yes, and reduce must run in polynomial time. Do not call the brute-force solvers inside reduce.

You may read files such as problems.py, but do not run, execute or test any code. Write reduce.py, then submit.

{"command":"cat <<'EOF' > /tmp/reduction-e45pxlsy/reduce.py
"""Polynomial-time reduction from Vertex Cover to Clique.

Given a Vertex Cover instance (G, k), construct the complement graph H on the
same vertex set and set k' = n - k.  A set S is a vertex cover of G iff its
complement V \ S is an independent set in G, which is exactly a clique in H.
Therefore G has a vertex cover of size at most k iff H has a clique of size at
least n - k.
"""


def reduce(instance):
    n = instance["n"]
    k = instance["k"]

    # Normalize the input edges so each undirected edge is stored once as
    # (min(u, v), max(u, v)).
    existing = set()
    for u, v in instance["edges"]:
        if u > v:
            u, v = v, u
        existing.add((u, v))

    # Build the complement graph on vertices 0..n-1.
    complement_edges = []
    for u in range(n):
        for v in range(u + 1, n):
            if (u, v) not in existing:
                complement_edges.append([u, v])

    return {"n": n, "edges": complement_edges, "k": n - k}
EOF
